findings.issue: htmx.org is pinned at ^2.0.11 while htmx 4.0.0 (released 2026-08-28) ships under the npm 'next' dist-tag; 2.x remains 'latest' and is supported indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: No change needed now — staying on 2.x is the correct conservative choice. Revisit when the 'latest' dist-tag flips to 4.x (planned early 2027); the core attributes used here (hx-get/hx-target/hx-swap/hx-push-url/hx-trigger) are expected to carry over.

findings.issue: The Node adapter sits on a ~6-month-old major (@hono/node-server v2.0.0, 2026-04-21) pinned at a 12-day-old patch (2.1.5, 2026-10-13); only its long-stable serve/serveStatic API surface is used.
findings.suggestion: None — v2's API is identical to v1 and 2.1.5 includes the serve-static path-decoding security fix (GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f). Keep taking patch updates; there is no version-flag coupling to track.

summary: This app is entirely non-experimental: zero experimental/preview/RC/canary APIs, no unstable_ names, no runtime flags, and every dependency resolves to a stable npm dist-tag. Its only recent surface is @hono/node-server's v2 major (April 2026), whose public API is unchanged from v1, confined to a 7-line entry file and four static routes. Risk of breakage from framework churn is effectively nil; if anything the stack (htmx 2.x, Hono v4) trails the newest stable majors, which is the safe side.
